title: Competing hypothesis generation (foundational)
description: For a puzzling observation, the explorer generates multiple competing explanations, deliberately including ones that contradict the current favorite. Generation is seeded from known mechanism families so hypotheses stay plausible rather than fanciful. The set is kept small, three to five, because each one must earn its evidence. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Hypothesis Explorer practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

t: Evidence retrieval for and against each (foundational)
title: Evidence retrieval for and against each (foundational)
description: Each hypothesis gets its own evidence search: queries are phrased to find both supporting and refuting records. A hypothesis that only ever seeks confirmation is flagged for confirmation bias. The explorer records hits on both sides so the tally reflects the real evidentiary balance. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Hypothesis Explorer practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Weighted evidence tally per hypothesis (foundational)
description: Supporting and refuting evidence are tallied with weights for source reliability and recency, producing a net score per hypothesis. A single strong refutation outweighs several weak supports, encoding the scientific asymmetry that falsification is decisive. Scores are comparable across hypotheses because they use the same weighting scheme. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
hypos = {'H1': ([0.8, 0.6], [0.9]), 'H2': ([0.5], [0.4, 0.7])}  # (supports, refutes)
for h, (s, r) in hypos.items():
    net = sum(s) - 1.5 * sum(r)  # refutations weigh more
    print(h, 'net score:', round(net, 2))
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Hypothesis Explorer practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Crucial-test search: evidence that discriminates (foundational)
description: The explorer prioritizes finding crucial tests: single pieces of evidence that would strongly favor one hypothesis while disfavoring another. A crucial test is worth more than ten confirmatory finds because it actually separates the contenders. When no crucial test exists in the archive, the explorer says so plainly instead of pretending the tally is decisive. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Hypothesis Explorer practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Explanation ranking with uncertainty (foundational)
description: Hypotheses are ranked by net score, but the ranking ships with explicit uncertainty: evidence counts, strongest refutation, and whether a crucial test was found. A ranking without uncertainty invites overconfidence, so the explorer refuses to present one. The top hypothesis is labeled 'leading', never 'proven'. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Hypothesis Explorer practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.
